title: Professional and Service Calls
goal: Identify yourself and your purpose, manage a transfer or message, and confirm what happens after a call.

runs.text: I'm calling about…
states the subject.
I'm calling regarding…
is another, more formal-sounding choice.
Could I speak with…?
requests a person. Both “Hi” and “Hello” can open a professional call; give enough identity and purpose for the task rather than relying on an elaborate greeting.

study.title: Start and get to the right person

turns.speaker: Receptionist

runs.text: Cedar Design, this is Morgan.

turns.en: Cedar Design, this is Morgan.

turns.speaker: Caller

runs.text: Hi, this is Lee Park from Harbor Print. Could I speak with Dana about the poster order?

turns.en: Hi, this is Lee Park from Harbor Print. Could I speak with Dana about the poster order?

turns.speaker: Receptionist

runs.text: I'll transfer you. May I put you on hold?

turns.en: I'll transfer you. May I put you on hold?

turns.speaker: Caller

runs.text: Yes, thank you.

turns.en: Yes, thank you.

turns.speaker: Receptionist

runs.text: Thanks for waiting. Dana isn't available. Can I take a message?

turns.en: Thanks for waiting. Dana isn't available. Can I take a message?

turns.speaker: Caller

runs.text: Please ask Dana to call me about the delivery date.

turns.en: Please ask Dana to call me about the delivery date.

blocks.caption: Start and get to the right person · Receptionist & Caller

runs.text: On hold
means waiting on the connection. A
transfer
changes whom you are connected to. If waiting is difficult: “I can't hold right now. Is there a callback option?” This gives the employee an alternative instead of assuming you must remain available.
Fictional message card: Lee Park, Harbor Print; order HP204; needs delivery-date confirmation before noon; callback 202-555-0146.

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Could you spell your name and give a callback number?

turns.en: Could you spell your name and give a callback number?

turns.speaker: Caller

runs.text: Lee Park—P-A-R-K. The number is 202-555-0146.

turns.en: Lee Park—P-A-R-K. The number is 202-555-0146.

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: And what's the message?

turns.en: And what's the message?

turns.speaker: Caller

runs.text: Please confirm the delivery date for order HP204. I'd appreciate a reply before noon if possible.

turns.en: Please confirm the delivery date for order HP204. I'd appreciate a reply before noon if possible.

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: I'll pass that on.

turns.en: I'll pass that on.

turns.speaker: Caller

runs.text: Thank you. Could you read back the order reference?

turns.en: Thank you. Could you read back the order reference?

runs.text: A request for a deadline does not guarantee a response. “It's urgent for our planning” gives a reason. “They know where to reach me” may work when contact information is genuinely known; a concrete callback detail is useful when it is not.

study.title: Customer service and a missing answer

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: How can I help?

turns.en: How can I help?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: I'm calling about an order marked delivered. I haven't received it.

turns.en: I'm calling about an order marked delivered. I haven't received it.

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: I'll check the record. What's the reference?

turns.en: I'll check the record. What's the reference?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: HP204. I've already contacted support once.

turns.en: HP204. I've already contacted support once.

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: We need to investigate and get back to you.

turns.en: We need to investigate and get back to you.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: When should I expect an update, and how will you contact me?

turns.en: When should I expect an update, and how will you contact me?

blocks.caption: Customer service and a missing answer · Agent & Customer

runs.text: “Could I speak with someone who can review this?” requests another level of help. “I need a clear next step” is firmer than merely repeating thanks. Explain the problem without inventing an outcome or using hostility as the only way to be heard.

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: Is there anything else?

turns.en: Is there anything else?

turns.speaker: Caller

runs.text: No, that's all. So you'll send an update by email after checking the order?

turns.en: No, that's all. So you'll send an update by email after checking the order?

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: Yes, I'll confirm the arrangement in the message.

turns.en: Yes, I'll confirm the arrangement in the message.

turns.speaker: Caller

runs.text: Thanks for your help. Goodbye.

turns.en: Thanks for your help. Goodbye.

blocks.caption: End with the arrangement · Agent & Caller

runs.text: Other endings: “I appreciate your time.” “I'll wait for that confirmation.” “Please contact me if you need more details.” Choose a closing that matches what actually happened; don't say the issue is resolved if it is still open.
Use the message card to ask for Dana. Partner says “Dana isn't available.” Leave your identity, reference, request, and callback details.
Partner reads HP240 instead of HP204. Correct the reference and request confirmation.
Use the missing-order case. Partner says an investigation is needed. Ask about timing and the channel for an update, then close without pretending the parcel has been found.
Solo: read receptionist or agent turns and speak the caller turns; later hide the card and reconstruct the message. All contact details are fictional and need not be called.
Possibilities:

“It's HP204—two, zero, four.” “When will I hear from you?” “Thank you; the issue is still open, so I'll look for the update.” Check whether the recipient knows who called, why, how to respond, and what remains unresolved.

vocabulary.ja: ダナさんと話せますか？

ja: 名乗り、用件、折り返しの確認。
note: 誰が何のために電話したかを最初に伝えます。伝言には必要な連絡先を添え、最後に次の対応を確認します。
